issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may set aside an acquittal on a private complainant’s application only within the narrow limits governing exceptional interference with acquittals.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused after accepting that workers had damaged neighbouring huts by mistake and finding no criminal intent proved.
On the private complainant’s revision, the High Court relied on circumstances it considered inconsistent with mistake, set aside two acquittals, and ordered a retrial.

The evidence included testimony that the accused had initially told the workers to stop, no direct evidence of instigation before the damage began, and accounts that did not distinguish between the accused.
The Supreme Court considered that the evidence could reasonably be disbelieved and that the revisional judge had not addressed the factors governing interference with an acquittal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in interfering in revision. The Supreme Court set aside its order and restored the trial court’s acquittals of the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: Revisional powers to set aside an acquittal on a private party’s application must be exercised very sparingly; a different possible view of the evidence is not enough. The court must find the circumstances warranting interference identified in D. Stephens v. Nosibolla, Logendranath Jha v. Polailal Biswas, and Harihar Chakravarty v. State of West Bengal. The judgment also notes that a private complainant has no right of appeal in such a case, although the law provides for appeals against acquittals.

rule.if: private_revision_against_acquittal and trial_court_acquitted_for_lack_of_intent and testimony_permitted_reasonable_disbelief and (revisional_judge_reweighed_evidence or revisional_judge_omitted_required_factors)

predicates.private_revision_against_acquittal: A private complainant sought revision of an acquittal rather than pursuing an appeal.
predicates.trial_court_acquitted_for_lack_of_intent: The trial court acquitted the accused after finding that criminal intent had not been proved.
predicates.testimony_permitted_reasonable_disbelief: The testimony contained circumstances, including the accused’s initial direction to stop the workers and the absence of direct evidence of prior instigation, that permitted a judicial mind reasonably to disbelieve the allegation.
predicates.revisional_judge_reweighed_evidence: The revisional judge relied on a different assessment of the evidence to set aside the acquittal.
predicates.revisional_judge_omitted_required_factor: The revisional judge did not address the factors governing when an acquittal may be disturbed in revision.

issues.definition: When a private complainant seeks revision of an acquittal for lack of intent, the testimony permits reasonable disbelief, and the revisional judge reweighs the evidence or omits the required factors, interference with the acquittal is unwarranted.
